steps.title: Open the home page
steps.narration: Let's start by opening the application home page. You should see the dashboard with a ready badge at the top.
steps.point_out: The badge in the top right reads 'Ready' with a green dot, and the page displays 'provider: seed'.

steps.title: Navigate to the Data Manager
steps.narration: The Data Manager is where you run backfill jobs to ingest historical data. Navigate there to see the job controls.
steps.point_out: The page shows 'Data Manager' and includes a 'Start a fetch / backfill job' section with date input fields and a 'Run history' section below.

steps.title: Start a focused backfill job
steps.narration: We'll run a small backfill for a single day to show how the system accepts and processes these requests quickly.
steps.point_out: After clicking Start, the Job progress panel shows the job moving through its lifecycle. The badge at the top stays 'Ready' throughout.

steps.title: Set the end date and start the job
steps.narration: We're setting both the start and end date to the same day (May 2nd, 2026) to show a focused, single-day backfill.
steps.point_out: The 'Start' button becomes active once both dates are filled in. The job begins executing immediately when you click it.

steps.title: Click the Start button
steps.narration: Now we start the job. The system will fetch or compute the data for that date range.
steps.point_out: The Job progress panel updates as the job runs. You can see the badge staying 'Ready' and available the whole time.

steps.title: Show pages load efficiently
steps.narration: One of this iteration's focuses is making sure every page in the application loads only the data it needs. Let's tour the main pages.
steps.point_out: The home page, Stocks list, and individual stock pages all load promptly with their expected content.

steps.title: View a specific stock
steps.narration: We can drill down into individual stocks. Here's Apple (AAPL) as an example—the page loads with all the stock information.
steps.point_out: The page heading shows 'AAPL' and the data loads efficiently.

steps.title: View the Sectors page
steps.narration: The Sectors page shows how stocks are organized by sector. Each page loads only the data needed to display that view.
steps.point_out: The page title shows 'Sectors' and the page renders promptly without loading unnecessary data.

steps.title: View the Backtest evidence page
steps.narration: The Backtest page shows the forward-tested evidence from our backtesting system. This page always serves pre-computed results, never makes you wait for fresh computation.
steps.point_out: The page shows 'Forward-tested evidence' and displays the backtesting results.

steps.title: Check background compute disclosure
steps.narration: When heavy data processing happens in the background, the application tells you about it. Let's see the Background Compute panel on the Data Manager page.
steps.point_out: The Background Compute panel on the /data page explains what background work is happening and notes that it is process-lifetime only—it clears on restart.

steps.title: Confirm the badge stays responsive
steps.narration: Even while backfills and background work run, the top-right readiness badge stays responsive and honest. It shows 'Ready' for a healthy backend, 'Checking backend…' while verifying, or 'Backend unavailable' if the service is down.
steps.point_out: The badge at the top right consistently shows a clear status—either 'Ready', initializing, or explicitly 'Backend unavailable', never a blank or confusing header.
